scenes.title: Hub restart
scenes.caption: What to do when the internet stops working.
scenes.say: When the internet stops working, restarting the hub often sorts it. Here's how, step by step.

scenes.title: One device?
scenes.caption: Check whether it is just one device first.
scenes.say: First, check it's not just one device. If your phone works on Wi-Fi but your laptop doesn't, restart the laptop instead.

scenes.title: Read the light
scenes.caption: Blue is working. Orange means the connection is lost.
scenes.say: Now look at the light on the front of the hub. Blue means all is well. Orange means it has lost its connection.

scenes.title: Off and on
scenes.caption: Switch it off, wait 30 seconds, switch it on.
scenes.say: Turn the hub off, at the back or the wall. Wait a full thirty seconds. Then turn it back on.

scenes.title: Be patient
scenes.caption: The light flashes for 2 to 3 minutes. Leave it alone.
scenes.say: The light will flash for two or three minutes while it reconnects. Don't turn it off again. When it's steady blue, try the internet.

scenes.title: Still stuck?
scenes.caption: Check the cable, then wait up to 10 minutes.
scenes.say: Still not working? Check the cable to the wall socket is pushed in at both ends. Orange for over ten minutes may mean a fault nearby.

picture.heading: STILL STUCK
items: Check status page on mobile data

scenes.title: Don't reset
scenes.caption: Leave the pinhole reset button alone, unless asked.
scenes.say: One warning. Don't press the pinhole reset button unless they ask you to. It wipes your Wi-Fi name and password, and every device needs setting up again.
